shared_elements: frontal standing/upright anthropomorphic figure carved on a monolithic upright slab
human face/head at the top occupying a broad rectangular field
headdress or headgear framing the head
carved motifs on the torso and lower body (belt-like or pendant elements)
circular disc motif on the torso
full-figure occupying the entire vertical face of the monument
justification: Both depict a single frontal, rigidly upright anthropomorphic figure filling the whole face of a tall vertical slab, with a broad head and headgear on top, arms folded across the chest, and disc/belt motifs on the torso below — a genuinely comparable overall scheme. They differ sharply in manner of depiction: A is densely covered with intricate, deeply undercut interlocking ornament, scroll-and-mask filler and elaborate fringed costume, while B is extremely spare and schematic, with a few shallow incised lines and a plain unadorned mass, so the specific motifs (masks, glyph-like fillers, feather fringes) of A have no counterpart in B.
